==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*bʰergʰ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|bargaynen||to bargain, make a pledge for sale}}, from {{der|en|fro|bargaigner|t=to bargain}}, from {{der|en|frk|*borganjan||to borrow, lend}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*burgijaną||to borrow, lend}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bʰergʰ-||to protect, secure}}. Akin to {{cog|goh|boragen|boragēn}}, {{m|goh|borgen|borgēn|to look after, care for}} ({{cog|de|borgen|}}), {{cog|ang|borgian||to borrow, lend, pledge}}. More at [[borrow]]. Compare {{cog|fr|barguigner}} and {{cog|pt|barganhar}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|bägən|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈbɑːɡən/|/-ɡɪn/}} * {{enPR|bärgən|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈbɑːɹɡən/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-bargain.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)ɡən|ɑː(ɹ)ɡɪn|s1=2}} * {{hyph|en|bar|gain}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party [[bind]]s themself to transfer the right to some property for a consideration, and the other party binds themself to receive the property and pay the consideration. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1883|author=J. J. S Wharton|title=Wharton's Law Lexicon |passage=A contract is a '''bargain''' that is legally binding.}} # An agreement or stipulation; mutual [[pledge]]. #: {{syn|en|contract|engagement|stipulation}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|III|ii|text={{...}}And when your honors mean to solemnize
The '''bargain''' of your faith, I do beseech you,
Even at that time I may be married too.}} # An item purchased for significantly less than the usual, or recommended, price #: {{syn|en|steal|[[deal]] (informal)}} #: {{ant|en|rip-off}} # A gainful transaction; an advantageous purchase. #: {{co|en|to buy (something) at a '''bargain'''}} #: {{ux|en|At that price, it’s not just a '''bargain''', it’s a steal.}} #* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|I|0016 |passage=Thus the red damask curtains which now shut out the fog-laden, drizzling atmosphere of the Marylebone Road, had cost a mere song, and yet they might have been warranted to last another thirty years. A great '''bargain''' also had been the excellent Axminster carpet which covered the floor;{{nb...}}.}} # The thing stipulated or purchased. #: {{syn|en|purchase}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|V|ii|text=If he say so, may his pernicious soul Rot half a grain a day! He lies to th' heart. She was too fond of her most filthy '''bargain'''.}} ====Derived terms==== {{col3|en|title=Terms derived from ''bargain'' (noun) |bargain basement |bargain hunter |Bargaintown |Faustian bargain |into the bargain |sell bargains |strike a bargain |Dutch bargain|Queen's hard bargain|Smithfield bargain|bargain and sale|bargain bin|bargain bucket|bargain-basement|catching bargain|drive a hard bargain|fool's bargain|in the bargain|keep one's side of the bargain|make the best of a bad bargain|plea bargain|plea-bargain|rue-bargain|time bargain|wet bargain| time-bargain|bargainer|bargainor|bargainous|prebargain}} ====Descendants==== * {{desc|srn|barki}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|agreement or contract concerning sale of property|deal}} * Afrikaans: * Arabic: * Basque: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Macedonian: * Naga: * Norman: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|сде́лка|f}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Telugu: * Ukrainian: * Welsh: * Yiddish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|agreement or stipulation;
